faq.q: What does it mean to see resistance as an ally?
faq.a: It means treating fear, hesitation, and difficulty as useful information and training rather than as a reason to quit. Friction often appears right before meaningful growth.

faq.q: Why do I feel resistance before doing something important?
faq.a: Important actions carry risk to our comfort, pride, or sense of identity, so the mind pushes back. The stronger the pull of something meaningful, the stronger that pushback can feel.

faq.q: Who said “the obstacle is the way”?
faq.a: The idea comes from Marcus Aurelius, who wrote in his Meditations that “what stands in the way becomes the way.” Ryan Holiday later used the phrase as the title of his book.

faq.q: How do I know if resistance is a warning I should listen to?
faq.a: Ask whether the action conflicts with your values, whether you’re truly exhausted, and whether you’d regret not trying. Resistance rooted in values or real depletion deserves to be heard.

faq.q: What is the fastest way to get past resistance?
faq.a: Make the first step so small it feels almost silly, such as writing one sentence or walking for ten minutes. Starting is usually the hardest part.

faq.q: Does resistance ever go away completely?
faq.a: Usually not. It tends to return at every new level of growth, which is a sign you’re still stretching rather than a sign that something is wrong.
